items.title: Epic CEO Tim Sweeney suggests AI could've saved Destiny 2 and will "enable games like Destiny to thrive!"
items.summary: Fresh off his fight with Valve over Steam AI labels, Tim Sweeney claims AI tools could have rescued Destiny 2's content pipeline and will let live-service games like Destiny 'thrive' by making content production dramatically cheaper and faster.
items.why: New, distinct Sweeney claim that AI is the fix for live-service content droughts — concrete AI x game-production argument from the Unreal/Fortnite boss, extending but not duplicating the published Sweeney/Valve disclosure cluster.
items.notes: Related to the already-published Sweeney/Valve Steam-labels cluster but a separate statement (Destiny 2 content pipeline). Curator should confirm it reads as a new beat, not a rehash.

items.title: Iron Lung and Dusk creator says using generative AI in games is great if you want "a big neon sign for your audience that says 'I don't give a f***'"
items.summary: Indie horror auteur David Szymanski (Dusk, Iron Lung) says shipping generative-AI content in a game signals to players that the developer doesn't care, arguing craft and intent are the whole point of indie games.
items.why: Sharp, quotable indie-developer verdict on gen AI as an anti-craft signal, from a creator with real cachet — complements the studio-level pushback stories already run without overlapping them.
items.notes: Distinct from the published devs-genai-pushback roundup and Gaider 'virulent plague' cards; same theme, new voice and new article.

items.title: Study uses Age Of Empires 2's scenario editor to illustrate why it's 'farcical' to treat AI as cognizant
items.summary: Researchers used Age of Empires 2's scenario editor as a test bed to show how easily LLM-style AI fails at basic situated reasoning, arguing it is farcical to treat current AI systems as conscious or truly cognizant.
items.why: A game engine repurposed as an AI-cognition laboratory — unusual research angle that flips the usual 'AI in games' framing and gives the games section a science beat.
items.notes: By John Walker. No other allowed-domain outlet found covering the study; no overlap with published cards.

items.title: Data analyst finds 'AI stigma' on Steam can reduce the number of reviews a game gets by around 53% — and the reviews it does get are more negative
items.summary: A data analyst crunched Steam data and found games carrying AI-content disclosures get roughly 53% fewer reviews, and the reviews they do get skew more negative — hard numbers for the commercial cost of shipping with AI on Steam.
items.why: First quantified evidence of the 'AI stigma' the Sweeney/Valve fight is about — data-driven counterpart to the disclosure-war stories already published, not a rehash of them.
items.notes: Oldest item in the pool (~12.5 days at publish); distinct from published Steam-label plugin and Next Fest disclaimer cards. Verify age tolerance at curation.

items.title: Steam Week in Review: spammy, AI-generated capsule art is a pox, and it makes browsing Steam less fun
items.summary: PC Gamer's Steam column argues AI-generated store capsule art has become a spammy plague on Steam's storefront, degrading discovery and making browsing the store visibly worse.
items.why: Storefront-level AI-slop angle (capsule art and discovery) not covered by any published card; gives the section a player-facing texture story.
items.notes: Weekly opinion column rather than hard news — lowest priority of the five; drop first if the section only needs 3-4 cards.
